extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the Hertz Fellowship (U.S. college seniors, first-year graduate students, or gap-year applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Eligibility and selection criteria for applying to the Hertz Fellowship: who may apply, what fields and degree plans are acceptable, and the attributes the Foundation looks for when selecting fellows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant academic status
rubrics_metrics.description: All eligible applicants must be college seniors, first-year graduate students, or in a gap period preparing to apply to graduate school.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended degree and enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must intend to pursue a full-time, in-person PhD in the applied physical and biological sciences, mathematics or engineering at an institution in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PhD must be full-time and in-person at a U.S. institution; see participating schools for institutional agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fields of study
rubrics_metrics.description: Hertz Fellowships are awarded to graduate students pursuing a PhD in the applied physical and biological sciences, mathematics or engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation does not award fellowships based on an applicant’s particular field of study; applicants must demonstrate how their field will be applied to address real‑world challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on solving major, near-term societal problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must intend to direct their studies toward understanding and solving major, near-term problems facing society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This could mean inventing a new technology, developing a business or applying interests in innovative ways. It is up to the applicant to advocate for their specific field of study and demonstrate application to high-impact, real-world challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. citizenship or permanent residency
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be citizens or permanent residents of the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of professional degrees (degree-type limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation does not award fellowships to applicants pursuing professional degrees other than a PhD, such as an MD, JD, MBA, DPH, or DVM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: the Foundation will support the PhD portion of an MD/PhD program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discrimination policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation does not discriminate against any individual on the basis of sex, race, creed, religion, color, gender, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, registered domestic partner status, age, sexual orientation, military and veteran status, or any other basis protected by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deep, integrated scientific and technical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Looking for applicants with deep scientific and technical knowledge who can drive the exploration of complex, multidisciplinary topics and who can clearly articulate their ideas during in-person conversations with interviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grades and test scores only tell part of the story; evaluators seek evidence of depth and integration of knowledge and the ability to explain ideas verbally in interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative problem solving
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should be creative problem solvers who can bring together expertise, resources, and critical thinking from different fields to create a solution far greater than the sum of its parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on multidisciplinarity and novel approaches rather than relying solely on conventional methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to the greater good
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should be directing their talents toward solving real-world problems that impact the nation and the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors those whose work has clear potential societal benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates should be self-starters who can gain the trust of colleagues, build consensus around an ambitious vision, and deliver on that promise down to the details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership evaluated as practical ability to lead projects and teams to achieve long-term goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated record of achievement (lifelong achievers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Looking for rising stars with a track record of success every step of the way—and a desire to grow in the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include innovative undergraduate research, excellence in extracurriculars (e.g., ROTC), or advancing a cause; evaluators value consistent evidence of high achievement and upward trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral commitment to make skills available in national emergency (non-binding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before awarding a fellowship, applicants are required to make a non-binding moral commitment to make their skills available to the United States in times of national emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is explicitly non-contractual: the Foundation does not define 'national emergency' and leaves judgment to each fellow about whether and when to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participating schools and institutional agreement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation has agreements with more than 50 U.S. universities to coordinate paying stipend, tuition, and other costs via a 9-month stipend model; if an awardee's school is not on the list, the applicant may ask to have it added and the Foundation will attempt to negotiate an agreement. Fellows may change to another participating school at any time during their fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should verify whether their intended PhD institution is a participating school; non-listed schools can be requested for addition but may require negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding for finalists at partner institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation has partnered with Case Western Reserve University and Texas A&M University to offer the full financial benefits of a Hertz Fellowship to applicants that advance as Hertz Finalists but are not ultimately selected as Hertz Fellows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalists should review partner-institution program details for eligibility and benefits.
